clue.text: Sixty per cent of left-wingers in the party

indicators.note: of a ten-letter word, sixty per cent keeps only the front six letters and drops the last four

parts.note: left-wingers are socialists

explanation.surface: A remark about how many of those at a gathering are on the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, chiming with left-wingers, but it is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a friendly gathering, as in a church or club evening, is a synonym of party.

clue.text: Team members getting weapons

parts.note: a side is a team
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Players on a team are being issued with guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' reads as team players but means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols or swords worn at the hip are weapons carried at one's side.

clue.text: Acclaimed Oxford course third- rate boy's kept outside

parts.note: third-rate is grade C

indicators.note: the boy is kept around the outside of the course

parts.note: a lad is a boy; the 's is boy is
PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a famous Oxford degree

explanation.surface: A boy studying a well-known Oxford degree gets cheered despite second-rate work.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree taken by many British politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeted with applause, a synonym of acclaimed.

clue.text: Chain of islands in a ring?

parts.note: a toll is the ring of a bell

explanation.surface: A question whether a string of islands forms a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the reef's shape, but here it is a bell's sound; the '?' marks the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon, often a chain of islets.

clue.text: One very quietly enters Herts town, making a short journey

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the letters for one and very quietly sit within the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire
one is the Roman numeral I
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slips silently into a Hertfordshire town on a brief outing.
explanation.walkthrough: TRING is a small town in Hertfordshire (Herts), north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a trip means taking a brief excursion, so the participle matches the phrase.

clue.text: Dodgy hotel in Paris for love affair

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A shady Parisian hotel is the setting for an illicit romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' looks like a French word clue, but its letters simply join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic or sexual involvement between two people, a broader word for an affair.

clue.text: Severely criticise mischievous goddess with everything going up in smoke

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and folly

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Slating a troublesome goddess makes everything vanish in a puff.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin cigar, and a cigar is colloquially a smoke.

clue.text: A Latin, I fancy, could be someone from Lazio

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so these letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a speaker of Latin might be from the region around Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazio is the region around Rome, so its natives are nationals of that country.

clue.text: A bird, look!

definitions.meaning: informal noun for a look, as in take a quick glance

explanation.definitionFit: The male goose bears this name, and in slang a quick glance is having one.

clue.text: What dolled-up pantomime dame has, as fiery character

definitions.meaning: a pantomime dame is a man in women's clothes, so he has ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame in full costume is cast as a hot-tempered figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime dame is a man in women's clothes, a British Christmas theatre tradition; such a costume is drag.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing legendary monster is literally a fiery creature, and figuratively a fierce person.

clue.text: Insect tucked into unattractive banana-like fruit

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, so the insect goes within the word for unattractive

parts.note: plain means homely or unattractive
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug has burrowed into an ugly tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy cooking fruit resembles a large banana and is a staple in Caribbean and African cooking.

clue.text: Classes sneer nastily, showing a lack of attention

indicators.note: nastily suggests the words are mangled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Upper classes scoff unkindly, revealing they are not paying heed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedlessness or negligence is the state of not paying proper attention.

clue.text: Plan plate to be prepared for party in court

indicators.note: the letters of plan and plate are to be made ready in a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to draw up a plan and get the dishes ready for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration, but here it means one side in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A person bringing an appeal is one of the litigants in a higher court hearing.

clue.text: The alcoholic drink he avoided — it gives wind

indicators.note: the word he is avoided, so those two letters are left out of the phrase

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone skipped the booze, which supposedly causes flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as gas but is the verb meaning to coil or twist.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to coil or twist round something is to wind it.

clue.text: One male leopard, ill- constructed sort of toy

indicators.note: badly built, so the letters of the phrase are put together in a different order

explanation.surface: A lone male big cat is oddly built, like some kind of plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-scale flying craft built by hobbyists is a classic toy or kit.

clue.text: Thus learn about Martin's followers

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: This is how the disciples of someone named Martin get educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Protestant church founded on the teachings of Martin Luther follow him.

clue.text: Male family members upset mum in America

parts.note: uncles are male relatives

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ma is mum, mother

explanation.surface: Uncles in the States have annoyed their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks emotional but reverses MA to AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat is the national personification of the United States.

clue.text: It's another wet start to afternoon, possibly? Get that info from here

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way
the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about yet another rainy afternoon and asks where the forecast comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorological readings such as rainfall are gathered at such a site, so it is where weather info comes from.

clue.text: Pornography in old books collected by Heather?

indicators.note: one piece is gathered up inside the other

parts.note: erica is the botanical genus of heather
OT, the Old Testament, is the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather has amassed a stash of dirty old books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, genus Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature or art intended to arouse sexual desire is a refined name for pornography.

clue.text: 7 fellow, losing head, little chap to be pushed aside

indicators.note: the first letter is lost from the front of the word

parts.note: 7-down's answer describes someone from Lazio, so the fellow is a signor, Mr in that language
Ed is a short form of Edward, a little name for a chap

explanation.surface: A man from Rome loses his head and a small boy gets brushed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The '7' refers to the answer of 7-down; a fellow from there is SIGNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disregarded or overlooked is to be brushed aside.

clue.text: Art of man leading his people from bondage

definitions.meaning: a picture made from small tiles or pieces of glass

definitions.text: of man leading his people from bondage
definitions.meaning: relating to Moses, who led the Israelites out of Egypt

explanation.surface: A description of artwork about a liberator such as Moses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiled pictures are an art form, and the adjective for Moses, as in the law he gave, is the same word.

clue.text: Oxygen region — it's in a layer high up

definitions.text: it's in a layer high up

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a zone is a region

explanation.surface: A description of an oxygen-rich region found in a high atmospheric layer.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen forms a protective layer in the stratosphere, well above the ground.

clue.text: Cash plan I worked out for waterway

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone devised a financial scheme to fund a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal wide and deep enough for ocean-going vessels is an artificial waterway.

clue.text: Near where the bishop may live

definitions.meaning: the precinct round a cathedral, where clergy have homes

explanation.definitionFit: Nearby is one sense; the other is a cathedral precinct where bishops and canons reside.

clue.text: Excited adult, chum in row bouncing back

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the friend is placed in the noise
the word for row comes back towards the start, read in reverse

parts.note: din is a row or racket
a mate is a chum

explanation.surface: A grown-up and a pal get worked up during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow here, a noisy racket; 'bouncing back' turns it to NID before the friend goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and full of spirit, a synonym of excited.

clue.text: Rock singer not performing as a craftsman

indicators.note: not performing means the word for performing is taken away

parts.note: Jim Morrison of The Doors, or Van Morrison, rock singers
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: A rock vocalist retires from the stage to become an artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: The craftsman is William Morris, the Victorian designer of the Arts and Crafts movement.
explanation.definitionFit: William Morris was the leading designer-maker of the English Arts and Crafts movement.

clue.text: Most idiotic twerp put in top position

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a crest is the top, as of a hill
an ass is a twerp, a fool

explanation.surface: The stupidest fool has been promoted to the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning grossly stupid, so most idiotic.

clue.text: Old hag gives a smile, having trapped lord heartlessly

indicators.note: the smile holds something within it

parts.note: a beam is a broad smile

indicators.note: without its heart, only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: An old crone grins after capturing a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for an ugly old woman, a synonym of hag.
